messages:
morgan: Quick heads-up — on the canary for quantized-3b-awq-int8 we’re seeing an odd token bias in table->text outputs, especially numeric columns. :thinking:
sanjay: Can you paste an example?
morgan: Example from eval set: input table with numeric columns -> expected '42' but model outputs 'forty-two' or '42.0' inconsistently depending on batch size.
alayna: Is this only AWQ-int8 or also fp8/gptq variants?
morgan: Saw it primarily with AWQ-int8 and with our hybrid FP8+AWQ profile. GPTQ-int8 run didn’t show the same severity.
kevin: Do we have logs for kv-cache/batching sizes? I wonder if continuous batching is changing tokenization path.
morgan: Short log snippet: ```batch=8 seq=128 model=awq-int8 tokens_prev=24 next_token_prob_bias={'46':0.72,'forty-six':0.18} ```
sanjay: Huh. Looks like discrete token probability mass shifting. Could be quant noise on final LM head. Any pattern by prompt length?
morgan: Yes — more likely when prefix has many numeric literals and when prefix hits cache reuse path.
alayna: Could be FP remap when compiled kernels select fused-matmul variant. We changed kernel selection thresholds last week for small-seq perf.
kevin: Can we reproduce locally with quantized checkpoint + deterministic seed? If deterministic seeds differ across kernels we can bisect.
eval-bot: [eval] Ran small reproduce harness on awq-int8: pass=14 fail=7 — failures concentrated on table2text and numeric-normalization tests.
morgan: Plan: 1) run deterministic small-batch reproduce (batch 1..16) 2) try AWQ params: per-channel-scale vs per-tensor 3) run pure fp8 and gptq checkpoints for same inputs 4) push a canary rollback if regressions hit customer traffic
sanjay: I can take (1) and (2) today. Alayna, can you check kernel selection diff between canary and baseline?
alayna: On it. I’ll diff the kernel selection dump and compile flags. Expect a report in ~3 hours.
kevin: If we confirm kernel-triggered behavior, we should add a unit test that stubs kernel selection and verifies token distribution for numeric tokens.
morgan: Agreed. Also toggling batch-size-based routing (canary used dynamic routing) to force dedicated single-thread path might mitigate.
sanjay: Found one quick repro with script: ```python repro.py --model awq-int8 --seed 42 --batch 4 --input tests/table2text/numcase.json``` reproduces 'forty-two' instead of '42'.
morgan: Great — ship that to the bisect run. If we can bisect to a kernel or quant rounding change, we’ll put an emergency patch to force baseline kernel for canary customers.
eval-bot: [note] Flagging this thread as high-priority regression. Triage label assigned: "quant-numeric-bias"
kevin: FYI, if we add a quick postprocessor to canonicalize numeric tokens (normalize 'forty-two' -> '42') we can reduce customer impact while root cause is investigated. Not ideal but short-term mitigation.
alayna: I’ll also check FP8 path; if FP8 avoids it we might recommend FP8 profile for table-heavy workloads in the docs until fixed.
sanjay: Starting bisect now, will report any commit range.
morgan: Thanks team. Keep updates here. :thumbsup:
